transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-01 11:00 AM PT (UTC-8)
- Duration: ~52 min
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (NovoScale), Marcus (CTO), Priya (Security), Omar (SRE)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros then we'll dive into topology and burst behavior.
[00:08] Lena (NovoScale): Lena here. Thanks.
[00:10] Marcus (NovoScale): Marcus on.
[00:11] Priya (NovoScale): Priya.
[00:12] Omar (NovoScale): Omar here.
[00:15] Maya: Great. High level: we want to understand whether Dedicated makes sense for you and how to size reserved pools, warm pools, and fallbacks. Is that the main goal?
[00:22] Marcus: Yes. We're between hosted dedicated and a private install. Short term we lean Dedicated because of steady load plus bursts tied to campaigns. Critical things: per-team isolation and predictable tail latency.
[00:33] Samir (Redwood SE): When you say per-team isolation, do you mean physically separate nodes or logical separation with quotas?
[00:38] Lena: Physical if possible. Some teams touch regulated-ish data; legal wants hard fences. If not full physical, at least pinned node sets per team.
[00:47] Samir: Got it. On Dedicated we can allocate node pools per tenant and pin models to pools.
[00:52] Marcus: Also, we get weekly marketing spikes that are about 8x our baseline and last 15-30 minutes. Cold starts kill conversion, so we need a warm-first response under 1s ideally.
[01:05] Samir: Short answer: full cold start for a 30B+ model is usually several seconds; warm pool and KV priming shorten first-token to the hundreds of milliseconds. We can design a small always-on warm pool sized for first-surge, then scale out prewarmed nodes for the remaining burst.
[01:20] Priya: Security: if we stay with Redwood's hosted Dedicated, can we bring our own KMS keys? Also need audit logs retained one year and per-call metadata.
[01:29] Maya: For Private we support customer-managed KMS. For Hosted Dedicated we integrate with BYOK options depending on region and contract. Audit logs and retention can be configured as an add-on; we'll note formats.

Traffic profile discussion:
[01:45] Samir: Can you share numbers: baseline RPS, peak RPS, p95/p99 targets, token lengths?
[01:51] Lena: Baseline steady is ~120 RPS, peaks up to ~1.0-1.2k RPS during campaigns. Models are mostly 30B family, prompts average 300-400 tokens; a small set of long-context endpoints go to 8k tokens. p99 goal during bursts is <=500ms for short responses.
[02:13] Samir: That helps. For long-context calls batching behaves differently; we'll need to isolate those flows or give them dedicated capacity.
[02:21] Omar: If the reserved pool saturates, what happens to excess requests? Queued? Fail? Route to hosted fallback?
[02:27] Samir: We support policy-based behavior: queueing is limited due to latency SLOs; recommended patterns are failover to a smaller quantized variant or route to a hosted model. You can choose deterministic rules — e.g., route only specific routes to fallback.
[02:42] Lena: We need explicit allowed-fallback model list. Some models can't be used for fallback because of data leakage concerns.
[02:48] Maya: We'll prepare a template allowed-model list for you to fill out.

Warm-pool math and options:
[03:00] Samir: Rough numbers: for a 30B-ish model on A100-equivalent, cold start to usable is 8-20s depending on weight loading and KV priming; warm pool first-token latency after priming can be ~150-400ms. If sub-1s is a hard requirement, keep a small warm pool always on sized for the initial spike.
[03:22] Marcus: Cost-wise what's the delta keeping say one node warm 24/7 vs spinning up on demand?
[03:28] Maya: Ballpark: an idle pinned warm node can cost ~60-75% of an actively used node depending on billing; spinning up on-demand incurs startup latency and may cost less overall if spikes are rare. We'll include scenarios in pricing.

Eviction, failover, and chaos scenarios:
[03:45] Samir: Eviction on Dedicated is uncommon if you have reserved capacity; when it occurs we do soft-shedding per policy and then route to fallback. We can simulate losing 20-30% of nodes and show p95/p99 impacts and fallback volumes.
[03:58] Omar: We want a documented degradation playbook: which tenants get rate-limited first, how to shed batch jobs, and alerting thresholds.
[04:06] Samir: We'll provide a sample playbook and a suggested tiering: non-critical tenants shed first, background batch compactions after that, keep interactive paths prioritized.

Networking and compliance detail:
[04:20] Priya: Need VPC peering, no public egress for inference payloads, and flow logs to our SIEM. Also SAML/SSO and fine-grained API keys per-team.
[04:30] Maya: Hosted Dedicated supports VPC endpoints and private connectivity in major regions; flow logs can be exported to your collector. Token-scoped RBAC is supported and maps to API key scoping.

Quantization and quality:
[04:44] Lena: We'll want quantization recommendations that preserve our eval thresholds. Can Redwood run regression tests?
[04:49] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize can profile, recommend quantization strategies, and run evals against your test sets; we produce a quality-vs-cost tradeoff matrix.

Commercial/commitment questions:
[05:03] Marcus: We're not ready for a 12-month lock. Can we do a quarter-by-quarter ramp with options to convert to annual?
[05:09] Maya: Yes, we offer quarterly reserved contracts with lower discounts; we can propose a hybrid pilot then convert to annual once you hit a usage threshold.

Recap and next steps:
[05:20] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood to send dedicated pricing and warm-pool playbook; 2) Samir will run throughput baseline once you share model artifacts and a representative prompt set; 3) NovoScale to provide KMS/compliance excerpts and RPS logs.
[05:35] Marcus: Can we slot the baseline next week?
[05:38] Samir: Tue/Wed works for me as soon as we have the artifacts.
[05:42] Lena: We'll aim to deliver artifacts Monday EOD.
[05:45] Maya: I'll follow up with calendar invite and attach the intake templates.
